data.cultural_impact: The name Teklal is of Hindu origin, and while the specific meaning may not be widely recognized beyond Hindu communities, the name carries cultural importance through its association with the Hindu deity, Teketh, the God of Time. This association implies that the name Teklal holds the power to protect and bestow blessings, echoing the belief in the protective and preservative qualities of the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: In a deeper spiritual sense, the name Teklal represents a connection to the divine power of protection and blessings. By carrying this name, one is symbolically allowing the energy of Teketh to flow through them and manifest as protection and blessings in their own lives and in the lives of those around them. It is an manifestation of faith and trust in the divine, recognizing that time and change are in the hands of a higher power. In this way, the name Teklal serves as a reminder of the presence and power of the divine in one's everyday life.

historical_references.reference: Teklal was a Jain monk and a prominent leader of the Digambara sect around the 12th century AD in western India. He is also known for his major contributions to Jain textual literature, specifically the commentaries on the Agama texts and the compilation of the Sanskrit text 'Samayasara' which is a code of conduct for Jain monks.
historical_references.context: Jain monk and leader of the Digambara sect in western India, known for his contributions to Jain textual literature

historical_references.reference: Teklal was a Chalukya king who reigned in the late 7th century AD in present-day Karnataka, India. He is noted for his military campaigns against the Pallavas and is also the founder of the city of Badami, which was the capital of the Chalukya empire during his reign.
historical_references.context: Chalukya king who ruled in present-day Karnataka, India, known for military campaigns and founding the city of Badami
